page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for high-density compute and memory-intensive workloads. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, yielding a total of 320 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, meaning storage must be attached externally.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-threaded operations and memory bandwidth. The PassMark CPU score reaches 85,426.66, with extended instructions testing scoring 117,918.35, placing it in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong at 96,293.69. Memory read bandwidth for small cached blocks is exceptionally high at 7,649.82 GB/sec, while large-block uncached reads and writes reach 316.04 GB/sec and 135.84 GB/sec respectively. For language model tasks, prompt processing on a small 135M model achieves 10,308.98 tokens per second, and text generation reaches 377.14 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a high-density resource allocation where the cost is justified by the massive parallel processing capabilities of the four H100 GPUs and the substantial 960 GB memory footprint. The absence of local storage requires external volume configuration, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This server is highly suited for large-scale deep learning, LLM training and inference, complex scientific simulations, high-throughput database operations, and intensive parallel data processing pipelines.
